- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.37 to +0.43) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially -0.37 to -0.43) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts, then overcorrects.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true prices often dip below forecast 2–3 days after sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.03 to 0.10), model tends to overproject upward — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “over-shock”.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.37/0.43 spikes, model should not forecast >+2.0% above recent peak — cap growth to avoid overfitting.
